Compare candidate CV schemes using a common diagnostic

Source: R/audit.R
compare_cv_schemes.Rd

A, J1 and J2 are ranked by absolute value; W, U1 and U2 by value. All candidates use the same supplied covariance and target. Schemes within tolerance of the minimum are tied and receive equal selection probabilities. No observed target errors are used to select or break ties. When evaluating such a rule, average the individual tied schemes' losses with these probabilities; do not average their signed errors before taking absolute values.

Usage

compare_cv_schemes(
  locations,
  schemes,
  target,
  covariance = NULL,
  criterion = c("J2", "W", "J1", "A", "U1", "U2"),
  tolerance = 1e-12
)

Arguments

locations

Numeric two-column coordinates or projected spatial points.

schemes

A nonempty named list of candidate fold partitions.

target

A prediction_target() or target coordinates.

covariance

A covariance object or correlation function; required for correlation-based selection.

criterion

One of "J2", "W", "J1", "A", "U1", or "U2".

tolerance

Absolute numerical tolerance for ties, in criterion units.

Value

A spcv_comparison list with table (one row per scheme, diagnostics, criterion_value, selected, and selection_probability), individual audits, the selection criterion and tolerance.

Examples

xy <- cbind(seq_len(20) / 20, rep(c(0, 1), 10))
q <- prediction_target(rbind(c(0.2, 0.5), c(0.8, 0.5)))
schemes <- list(random = spatial_folds(xy, 4),
                block = spatial_folds(xy, 4, "block"))
compare_cv_schemes(xy, schemes, q, spatial_covariance(0.3, 0.8))
#> CV comparison by |J2| 
#>  scheme     W        J2 criterion_value selection_probability
#>  random 0.395 0.2977614       0.2977614                     0
#>   block 0.200 0.1074095       0.1074095                     1
